name: Wedding
tldr: 💒 announces a wedding or marriage; it is rarely just a casual symbol for romance or serious intentions.

contextMeanings.meaning: The chapel directly identifies a wedding ceremony and commonly accompanies a photo or announcement about getting married.
💒 can mark the wedding date in a save-the-date message, especially when the couple wants to share the news directly.
A colleague may use 💒 in a work chat when announcing their own marriage or sharing wedding news with coworkers.
contextMeanings.example: quick wedding announcement from our team 💒 congrats to them!

contextMeanings.meaning: If someone drops 💒 into an unrelated joke or casual chat, most readers may still treat it as a real marriage announcement.

platformNotes.note: In an Instagram caption, 💒 beneath wedding photos reads as a direct marriage announcement. Outside that setting, it can look like a declaration that does not belong in the post.
In a TikTok caption, pairing 💒 with ceremony footage or a date gives the post a clear wedding meaning. A stand-alone use may still be read as an announcement rather than decoration.

In a family or friend group on WhatsApp, “we did it 💒” is an efficient way to announce the marriage. Reactions often become congratulations because the emoji leaves little room for a casual interpretation.
In a Slack work channel, 💒 makes a colleague's personal announcement easy to recognize. Dropping it into an ordinary work conversation can be mistaken for news about an actual wedding.

generationalNotes.note: Gen Z often adds 💒 to compact Instagram captions and stacks it with emojis such as 🥂, 💐, or 🎉. The chapel keeps the post centered on the marriage while the extra symbols add the celebration.
Millennials are likely to treat 💒 as the practical announcement symbol in wedding and family chats. A date beside it, such as “💒 06.14.2026,” works like a concise save-the-date.
Gen X is unlikely to read 💒 as a subtle romantic hint. The chapel is most likely to be taken literally as news that a wedding or marriage has happened.

warnings.title: Casual use looks like a hard announcement
warnings.description: 💒 does not remain decorative in an unrelated group chat; readers may assume someone is announcing a marriage. Use ❤️ or another plainly casual symbol when no wedding is involved.

warnings.title: Wedding does not mean engagement
warnings.description: Using 💒 to signal that a relationship is becoming serious can be mistaken for news that the wedding has already happened. Use 💍 when the engagement is the actual announcement.

seoDescription: What does 💒 mean? It announces a wedding or marriage, marks a save-the-date or anniversary, and adds ceremony or celebration to wedding posts.

longForm.overview:
💒 is easy to misread because it sits close to several different relationship symbols: 💍 announces an engagement, 👰🤵 shows the couple at the ceremony, and 💑 can be mistaken for a relationship declaration. But 💒 itself has a much narrower job. Its chapel means a wedding or marriage announcement, especially when it appears with wedding photos, a date, or a celebration.

When someone posts “we did it 💒,” they are marking the marriage, not merely saying they like weddings. “one year married 💒” celebrates an anniversary, while “💒 06.14.2026” can label a save-the-date. The same goes for 💒 beside a wedding chapel: most readers will say the couple got married. Pair it with 🥂 or 🎉 and it adds a toast or loud celebration; add 💐 and the post foregrounds the flowers. That directness is useful, but it is why 💒 feels misplaced outside a wedding announcement. The chapel does not soften into casual intent, so a joke or stray use can look like a hard announcement.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
💒 shows up after the big photo dump, where a single emoji can stand in for a paragraph: “we did it 💒.” People also use it to label a save-the-date, mark the wedding day, or note an anniversary. In a group chat, “💒 06.14.2026” gives friends the essential date and ceremony reference without adding more detail.

It becomes more specific when paired. 💒💍 says the marriage and the rings, 💐💒 points out the flowers, and 🥂💒 or 🎉💒 turns the announcement into a celebration. 👰🤵 instead depicts the couple, while 💒 focuses on the wedding itself. These are announcement devices, not subtle hints: if the surrounding message is ambiguous, 💒 will still be read as “we are married.”
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Do not use 💒 for generic romance, a date invitation, or a playful comment about finding a spouse. A couple may think 💒 is a cute way to suggest serious feelings, but the chapel is commonly taken as a marriage announcement, not a soft hint. It can also land badly when dropped into an unrelated joke or a group chat where the sender expects the emoji to remain decorative.

If you mean engagement, use 💍 and let the surrounding words explain it. For the wedding day, 👰🤵 can show the couple, while 🎉, 🥂, or 💐 handle celebration and flowers. When no wedding is involved, skip 💒 rather than relying on context to rescue it. The safer choice is ❤️ or another plainly noncommittal symbol, depending on what you meant.
longForm.howToReply:
If a friend sends 💒, congratulate them: “congrats!! 💒” or “love this for you 💒.” Mirroring the chapel keeps the ceremony in focus; adding 🥂 turns your reply into a toast, while 🎉 makes it a louder celebration. For a save-the-date, acknowledge the date and ask about the plans rather than treating the emoji as proof the ceremony has already happened.

If 💒 lands on your own post and seems too strong, ask whether they meant a wedding announcement. If someone used it casually in a group chat, do not correct them aggressively; ask privately what they meant. The safest move is to check, because treating 💒 as a casual symbol can leave the sender wondering why their wedding announcement received real congratulations.

faqs.question: What does 💒 mean from a guy
faqs.answer: 💒 from a guy almost always points to a wedding or marriage, especially when it accompanies photos, a date, or “we did it.” It is not usually a private signal that he wants to get serious.

faqs.question: Is 💒 flirty
faqs.answer: 💒 can accompany a romantic announcement, but the chapel itself is not primarily flirty. Most readers will interpret it as “we are married” or “we are getting married,” even when the couple is excited and playful.

faqs.question: What does 💒 mean on TikTok
faqs.answer: On TikTok, 💒 usually marks a wedding announcement, ceremony clip, save-the-date, or anniversary post. Without wedding context, it can still be mistaken for real relationship news.

faqs.question: Can 💒 mean an engagement
faqs.answer: Use 💍 for an engagement. 💒 points more directly to the wedding or marriage, so the two emojis can mark different stages of the same story.

conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is announcing that they got married. Reply with congratulations and excitement rather than treating the emoji as a vague romantic hint.
The sender is sharing the wedding date with their partner. Acknowledge the date and celebrate the news; do not assume the ceremony has already happened.

conversationExamples.message: quick announcement: our coworker just got married 💒 congrats!
conversationExamples.interpretation: A coworker is sharing marriage news in the work chat. Congratulate them or react positively, while recognizing that a stray 💒 in an ordinary work discussion could confuse the room.
The sender is celebrating a first wedding anniversary. Reply with an anniversary message, not congratulations on the original marriage.
This is a wedding celebration post with the bouquet and chapel shown together. The sender is emphasizing both the flowers and the marriage, so an enthusiastic celebration fits.
